BBNI.body: Syndicated loan volume reached US$25.51 bn as of 1 Oct 2026, a 36.9% year‑on‑year increase despite a drop in the number of projects to 49 from 54. PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BNI) led the Mandated Lead Arranger list with US$4.23 bn across 20 projects, followed by PT Bank Mandiri Tbk with US$3.67 bn on 19 projects, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BRI) with US$2.40 bn on 14 projects, and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BCA) with US$1.54 bn on 13 projects. United Overseas Bank (UOB) and Oversea‑Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) recorded participation of US$1.31 bn on 9 projects and US$948.6 m on 7 projects respectively. Bank Jakarta partnered with PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (Persero) to provide Rp2.11 tn of syndicated financing for seven priority infrastructure projects in Jakarta, with Bank Jakarta contributing Rp1 tn. The article notes that infrastructure, energy, mining and especially data‑center projects are driving the strong demand for syndicated loans, though growth is expected to moderate toward year‑end.

BMRI.body: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) is viewed as still attractive to investors for its dividend policy, with a payout ratio of about 79% of net profit for fiscal year 2025. The bank distributed around Rp44.47 trillion in dividends from fiscal 2025 net profit of Rp56.3 trillion, and set a 2026 interim dividend of Rp6.16 trillion, or Rp66 per share, bringing total dividends paid or declared across calendar 2026 to about Rp50.63 trillion. BBRI.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Net Profit Grows 6.6% to August, Maybank Sekuritas Maintains Buy with Rp 3,900 Target
BBRI.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) posted bank-only net profit of Rp 34.8 trillion in the first eight months of 2026, up 6.6% year on year, supported by net interest income growth of 3.4% and pre-provision operating profit growth of 6.7%, even as net interest margin pressure persists. Loan outstanding reached Rp 1,447 trillion in August 2026, up 13.7% year on year, prompting management to raise its 2026 loan growth guidance to 8%-10% from 7%-9%, while cost of credit fell to 3.29% from 3.34%. Deposits grew 12.6% year on year to Rp 1,656 trillion, improving the loan-to-deposit ratio to 87.4% from 89.7% in July, though CASA slipped to 64.8% from 66.2% amid a shift toward costlier funding. Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia analyst Jeffrosenberg Chenlim maintained a buy recommendation with a target price of Rp 3,900 per share based on 1.8x 2026 price-to-book value, citing improving asset quality and declining provisioning costs.

BBRI.title: Indonesian Stock Market Slides 6.96% in September 2026 as Analysts Recommend Stocks for October Recovery
BBRI.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 6.96% month on month in September 2026, from 6,525.47 at the end of August to 6,071.13 at the end of September, pressured by the US Federal Reserve's 25 basis point rate hike to 3.75%-4.00%, a stronger US dollar, and oil prices that briefly touched US$132 per barrel. Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 1.95 trillion in a single session in early September, with PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) among the most sold stocks. Analysts recommend gradual accumulation in large-cap banking stocks including PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI), and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), gold and metal stocks PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), coal stock PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI), and consumer and plantation stocks PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT), PT Dharma Satya Nusantara Tbk (DSNG), and PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) for October 2026. Bank Indonesia held the BI-Rate at 5.75% in September to maintain exchange rate stability amid external pressures.

BBRI.title: Exporters Can Use Natural Resource Export Proceeds (DHE SDA) as Loan Collateral, Opening New Opportunities for Banks and Exporters
BBRI.body: Government Regulation No. 21 of 2026, effective September 2026, allows exporters to use natural resource export proceeds (DHE SDA) held at 15 designated banks as collateral for rupiah loans, with interest rates left to each bank's discretion. Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) and Bank Mandiri have already applied the scheme by disbursing Rp 6 trillion in loans to PT Bukit Asam Tbk (PTBA), comprising Rp 2 trillion in working capital credit from BRI and Rp 4 trillion in DHE SDA loans from Bank Mandiri for PTBA's operational needs. Analysts project demand will concentrate among large coal, palm oil, and mineral exporters, benefiting exporters through lower-cost rupiah liquidity without releasing dollars to the forex market, while banks gain low-risk lending backed by cash deposits. Risks include currency mismatch management, potential additional collateral demands if the rupiah strengthens sharply, and competition among the 15 banks raising funding costs; HSBC Indonesia has no DHE SDA-backed financing program yet but welcomes the policy.

BBRI.title: IHSG Plunges to 5,900 Level Amid Cabinet Reshuffle, Lowest in Over Two Months
BBRI.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell more than 1.61% to 5,973.16 on Thursday (October 1, 2026), its lowest level in over two months and first touch of the 5,900 zone since July 10, 2026, as President Prabowo Subianto reshuffled the Red and White Cabinet. Basic materials fell 2.72%, consumer non-primary 2.55%, and utilities 2.31%, with heavyweight decliners including PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN), PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), and PT DCI Indonesia Tbk (DCII). Foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp204.30 billion in session I, led by net sales of GOTO (Rp62.77 billion), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) (Rp29.52 billion), AMMN (Rp24.55 billion), BBRI (Rp19.80 billion), and PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) (Rp19.54 billion). The reshuffle saw Police General Listyo Sigit Prabowo appointed Presidential Chief of Staff, replacing TNI General Dudung Abdurachman, while Police General Suyudi Ario Seto became Kapolri and Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia moved to Coordinating Minister for Downstreaming and Energy.

BBCA.title: Assessing PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) stock outlook through end‑2026
BBCA.body: The article evaluates the outlook for PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) stock up to the end of 2026. On 2 Oct 2026 the share traded at Rp 6,100, up 1.67% intraday, while YTD the price has fallen about 24% and the week shows a 2.4% correction; net foreign selling reached roughly Rp 32.1 trillion YTD. Analysts note that despite the price decline, the bank’s fundamentals remain solid with profit growth, a strong CASA base, minimal micro‑credit exposure and quarterly dividends, which they view as price‑supporting factors. The stock faces pressure from foreign fund outflows, uncertainty ahead of the MSCI review in November, and the newly introduced short‑selling mechanism, but analysts maintain a buy recommendation, citing potential upside if MSCI status, Fed rate pauses, and rupiah stability improve.

BBCA.title: IDX Implements Short Selling and Intraday Short Selling Gradually Starting October 1, 2026
BBCA.body: PT Bursa Efek Indonesia (IDX) stated that the implementation of Short Selling and Intraday Short Selling (IDSS) transactions is being carried out gradually, taking into account the readiness of mechanisms, infrastructure, Exchange Members, and risk management. The initial phase, effective October 1, 2026, grants IDSS facility licenses to two Exchange Members, PT Ajaib Sekuritas Asia and PT Semesta Indovest Sekuritas, and covers five stocks in the Short Selling List: ASII, BBCA, BRPT, BUMI, and INDF, selected for their high free float and liquidity. Short Selling quotas are set per Exchange Member based on average daily transaction value in the Regular Market over the prior month: members with average daily value below Rp750 billion may short sell up to 0.02 percent of listed shares per day, those between Rp750 billion and Rp1.5 trillion up to 0.03 percent, and those above Rp1.5 trillion up to 0.05 percent. IDSS investors must deposit an initial margin of at least Rp50 million or 50 percent of the Short Selling transaction value, whichever is higher, with margin adequacy monitored via the Short Selling Ratio and a forced buy mechanism executed automatically at the end of each trading day for IDSS positions; a transition period allows domestic individual investors access to Short Selling until December 31, 2026.

BBCA.title: Indonesia Stock Exchange Reopens Short Selling: Can It Improve Stock Price Discovery?
BBCA.body: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) officially reopened short selling transactions on Thursday (1/10/2026), initially limiting the facility to five stocks: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT), PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI), and PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF), and to two bourse members. Mirae Asset Sekuritas Senior Market Analyst Nafan Aji Gusta said short selling can help improve price discovery and serve as a hedging instrument, though implementation should be gradual with strict oversight given high market volatility. BEI said short selling has the potential to increase market liquidity, with realization depending on future expansion of eligible stocks and bourse members. The analyst noted ASII and BBCA offer strong liquidity and market depth, BRPT and BUMI carry higher volatility and trading opportunity with higher risk, while INDF is a more defensive alternative, and advised investors to apply disciplined risk management given the theoretically larger losses if prices rise.

TLKM.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) offers premium buyback to dissenting shareholders after second‑phase spin‑off of its Wholesale Fiber Connectivity to PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia
TLKM.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) is proceeding with the second phase of spinning off its Wholesale Fiber Connectivity segment to PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia and is offering a buyback to shareholders who oppose the spin‑off. The buyback price is set at Rp2,290 per share, a premium to the closing price of Rp2,250 on 2 Oct 2026 and above the recent low of Rp2,310 on 29 Sep 2026 after the share price fell from around Rp2,400 earlier in the week. Shareholders who do not approve the spin‑off may submit sell‑back requests between 2 Oct and 5 Oct 2026, with payment to be made within seven business days after the Ministry of Law approves the capital increase of PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia. The spin‑off became effective on 1 Oct 2026, following the RUPSLB meeting on 30 Sep 2026 where the agenda was approved.

TLKM.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) Shares Break Key Support at Rp2,290, But Analysts Maintain Positive Outlook
TLKM.body: Shares of PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) fell 1.75% to Rp2,250, breaking a key daily and H4 timeframe support level at Rp2,290 that had not been breached since March 2025, with the stock down 35% year-to-date and an RSI of 17 indicating oversold conditions. Despite the decline, analysts remain positive on the state-owned telecommunications company. UOB Kay Hian Sekuritas identified two major catalysts, including the second-stage spin-off of network infrastructure assets to Telkom InfraCo (TIF), known as Infranexia, approved at Telkom's extraordinary general meeting of shareholders on September 30, 2026, with cumulative transaction value of around Rp49.9 trillion. The transaction consolidates Telkom's fiber connectivity business into TIF to increase scale ahead of a potential transaction with a strategic partner. TLKM.title: PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) Replaces Dian Siswarini as President Director After 16 Months, Appoints Nanang Hendarno
TLKM.body: An extraordinary general meeting of shareholders (RUPSLB) of PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) on 30 September 2026 replaced President Director Dian Siswarini, who had held the post for about 16 months since 27 May 2025, with Nanang Hendarno, previously Director Network. The company stated the change has no material impact on operational, legal, or financial activities, and no official reason was given, though sources suggested it may relate to internal reforms Dian initiated, including addressing alleged conflicts of interest and scrutiny over infrastructure capex of Rp20 trillion for Telkom and Rp15 trillion for Telkomsel. Other board changes include Budi Satria Dharma Purba becoming Director Network, Radita Ali Putra taking Budi's former Director Wholesale & International Service role, and Kharim I. G. Siregar replacing Faizal R. Djoemadi as Director IT Digital. In semester I-2026, TLKM posted net profit of Rp10.6 trillion, up 1.4% year-on-year, on consolidated revenue of Rp75.9 trillion, up 3.9%, with EBITDA rising 3.8% to Rp37.5 trillion (49.4% margin) and normalized net profit of Rp11.3 trillion, up 6.2%. Separately, Telkomsel, a subsidiary of TLKM, holds about 23.72 billion shares of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO), or 1.99% of shares outstanding, worth roughly Rp878 billion at Rp37 per share versus an acquisition value of about Rp6.40 trillion at Rp270 per share, an unrealized decline of about Rp5.53 trillion or 86.3%.

TLKM.title: PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk Spin-Offs Rp85.7 Trillion Fiber Network Business to Subsidiary InfraNexia in 'AI Ready' Strategy
TLKM.body: PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk has officially spun off its wholesale fiber connectivity business and assets to its subsidiary, PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia (InfraNexia), with independent shareholder approval at an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders on September 30. The transaction, valued at Rp85.7 trillion, transfers more than 90 percent of Telkom's network infrastructure assets, including 112,000 kilometers of fiber optic cable with 26,000 kilometers of inter-island submarine cable, making InfraNexia one of Indonesia's largest wholesale digital infrastructure providers. The spin-off is part of the TLKM 30 strategy, positioning Telkom as a Strategic Holding and InfraNexia as an operating company focused on network infrastructure management under a carrier-neutral, open-access model. InfraNexia aims to strengthen its role as AI Ready Infrastructure supporting AI, cloud, and data center growth, while the RUPSLB also approved changes to Telkom's board composition to support the transformation agenda.

TLKM.title: MITI Expands Silica Mining via CNEC INA Partnership, DEWA Sees New Contract Opportunities, and AALI Declares Interim Dividend

VKTR.title: PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR) Posts 56% Revenue Growth and Expands Electric Vehicle Business Through e-MaaS

The company is developing an Electric Mobility-as-a-Service (e-MaaS) model that shifts vehicle usage costs from capital expenditure to operational expenditure through periodic lease payments, reducing upfront investment for fleet operators. VKTR said the model expands its business from commercial electric vehicle sales toward mobility solutions, positioning it as an enabler helping customers adopt and operate electric vehicles across sectors such as public transport, logistics, plantations, industry, and mining.

MDKA.title: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) Offers Rp4.12 Trillion Bonds with Coupons up to 10%
MDKA.body: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) is offering Obligasi Berkelanjutan V Merdeka Copper Gold Phase IV Year 2026 bonds with a principal amount of Rp4.12 trillion, as part of a continuous public offering targeting Rp15 trillion, of which Rp6.10 trillion has previously been issued. Series A bonds total Rp1.81 trillion with a fixed 8.25% annual coupon and a 367-calendar-day tenor, maturing on October 27, 2027. Series B bonds total Rp2.31 trillion with a fixed 10% annual coupon and a three-year tenor, maturing on October 20, 2029. Interest is paid quarterly, with the first payment on January 20, 2027; the offering period runs October 14-15, 2026, with listing on the Indonesia Stock Exchange expected October 21, 2026. The bonds are unsecured but backed by all of the company's assets, rank pari passu with other creditors, and the company holds an option to buy back the bonds starting one year after the allotment date.

DSSA.title: Dian Swastatika Sentosa (DSSA) Strengthens Sinarmas Group's AI and Digital Infrastructure Ecosystem
DSSA.body: Dian Swastatika Sentosa (DSSA), part of Sinarmas Group, reported first-half 2026 revenue of USD1.77 billion, up 34 percent year-on-year, with profit attributable to owners of the parent rising 79.6 percent to USD174.4 million. DSSA.title: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) Posts 34% Revenue Growth in H1 2026 on Diversified Energy and Digital Strategy
DSSA.body: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), a Sinar Mas Group issuer, reported consolidated H1 2026 revenue of US$1.77 billion, up 34.0% year-on-year, with profit attributable to owners of the parent rising 79.6% to US$174.4 million. The energy pillar, through coal mining and trading, generated US$1.53 billion in revenue (up 29.8%), while the technology and digital infrastructure pillar posted US$182.2 million (up 89.3%). Growth initiatives include MoraRepublic's fiber-to-the-home expansion to 186 cities and regencies and its FWA service MyRepublic Air, plus the SMX01 AI-ready data center developed by SM+ with Korea Investment Real Asset Management (KIRA) and LG Sinar Mas, targeted to operate in Q4 2026. The company also merged MORA and PT Eka Mas Republik into PT Ekamas Mora Republik Tbk (MoraRepublic), formed an AI joint venture with iFLYTEK, and held cash and equivalents of US$723.3 million as of June 30, 2026, up 75.2% from end-2025.

DSSA.title: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) Net Profit Jumps Nearly 80% in First Half of 2026, Analyst Sees Continued Growth Prospects
DSSA.body: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), a holding company of Sinarmas Group, posted revenue of US$1.77 billion for January–June 2026, up 33.98% year on year, with net profit of US$174.35 million, up 79.59% YoY. Coal mining and trading contributed US$1.53 billion (up 29.78% YoY), while renewable energy revenue surged 153.91% YoY to US$176.97 million, cable TV and internet generated US$170.49 million (up 95.62% YoY), and digital solutions and data center lines added US$6.63 million and US$5.05 million respectively. Mirae Asset Sekuritas analyst Nafan Aji Gusta attributed the strong performance to mining strength plus growing non-mining contributions, and sees growth prospects through 2027 from digital infrastructure and sustainable energy, including the SMX01 data center project of over 18 MW and MoraRepublic expansion, though he flagged coal price volatility, large capital expenditure needs, and project execution risks. He recommended an "add" rating on DSSA with a target price of Rp 1,570 per share, versus the closing price of Rp 1,120 on Thursday (1/10/2026), up 4.67% from the previous day.

DSSA.title: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) Posts 79.6% Net Profit Growth in First Half of 2026
DSSA.body: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), a Sinar Mas Group company, reported first-half 2026 revenue of US$1.77 billion, up 34% year on year, with profit attributable to owners of the parent rising 79.6% to US$174.4 million. President Director Krisnan Cahya attributed the results to the company's diversification strategy, driven by growth in data, connectivity, and artificial intelligence demand. The mining and coal trading segment contributed US$1.53 billion (up 29.78%), renewables US$176,971 (up 153.91%), and cable TV and internet services US$170.49 million (up 95.62%), alongside digital solutions and data center revenues of US$6.63 million and US$5.05 million. MoraRepublic expanded its fiber-to-the-home network to 186 cities and regencies, while SM+, together with Korea Investment Real Asset Management and LG Sinar Mas, is completing the SMX01 AI-focused data center in Jakarta, targeted to begin operations in Q4 2026. DSSA is also developing renewables through the joint venture PT Daya Mas Bumi Sentosa with PT FirstGen Geothermal Indonesia and owns PT Trina Mas Agra Indonesia, which produces domestic solar cells and modules.

DSSA.title: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) Posts Rp2.9 Trillion Net Profit, Up 79.6%
DSSA.body: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) recorded a net profit of US$174.35 million (around Rp2.9 trillion) in the first half of 2026, up 79.6% from US$79.08 million a year earlier, on revenue of US$1.77 billion, up 34%. Most revenue came from coal mining and trading at US$1.53 billion, while cable TV and internet services grew to US$170.49 million from US$87.15 million. DSSA completed the acquisition of PT Bali Media Telekomunikasi (BMT), which holds a 24.57% stake in PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk (EXCL), giving DSSA indirect ownership in EXCL as part of its telecommunications and digital infrastructure expansion. Its digital segment posted first-quarter revenue of US$69.1 million, up 50%, boosted by the merger of PT Eka Mas Republik (MyRepublic Indonesia) and PT Mora Telematika Indonesia Tbk (Moratelindo) into PT Ekamas Mora Republik Tbk (MoraRepublic), with a fiber optic network of over 166,000 kilometers reaching more than 12.7 million homepass. Through PT SMPlus Digital Investama (SM+), DSSA is expanding data centers, including the Jakarta SMX01 flagship which reached topping off in May 2026 and 25 Edge Data Centers, and formed PT Brilian Teknologi Sejahtera in partnership with iFLYTEK for AI and machine learning solutions.

AMRT.title: Alfamart vs Indomaret: Comparing Profitability of Indonesia's Two Largest Minimarket Chains
AMRT.body: This article compares the financial performance of Indonesia's two dominant franchised minimarket chains, Alfamart and Indomaret, for the first half of 2026. Alfamart is managed by PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT), controlled by Djoko Susanto, which posted net revenue of Rp 67.95 trillion in H1-2026, up 6.48% from Rp 63.81 trillion a year earlier, with net profit attributable to owners of the parent of Rp 2.02 trillion, up 7.4% from Rp 1.88 trillion. AMRT.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 6.96% month on month in September 2026, from 6,525.47 at the end of August to 6,071.13 at the end of September, pressured by the US Federal Reserve's 25 basis point rate hike to 3.75%-4.00%, a stronger US dollar, and oil prices that briefly touched US$132 per barrel. AMRT.title: Government's Rp 31 Trillion Stimulus Seen Supporting Consumer Stocks AMRT, MIDI, ICBP, INDF, and MYOR
AMRT.body: The Indonesian government plans to roll out around Rp 31 trillion in economic stimulus in Q4-2026 to support household consumption, seen as a positive catalyst for consumer and retail issuers. The stimulus includes food aid of 10 kilograms of rice per month for three months for 33.24 million beneficiary families in deciles 1-4 with a budget of Rp 17.5 trillion, and wage subsidy assistance (BSU) of Rp 300,000 per month for three months for about 13.3 million workers with a budget of nearly Rp 12 trillion, plus a planned account-opening program for citizens above 17 years old in deciles 1-4. Analyst Ekky Topan of Infovesta Kapital Advisori views retail issuers AMRT and MIDI as well-positioned due to wide store networks selling daily necessities, while consumer staples issuers ICBP, INDF, and MYOR are seen as attractive for their strong brands and broad distribution. His top picks are ICBP with a target price of Rp 9,500-10,500, AMRT at around Rp 2,100, and MYOR at Rp 2,700-2,850, with a preference for gradual accumulation on strong fundamentals rather than chasing stimulus-driven rallies.

PTBA.title: Exporters Can Use Natural Resource Export Proceeds (DHE SDA) as Loan Collateral, Opening New Opportunities for Banks and Exporters
PTBA.body: Government Regulation No. 21 of 2026, effective September 2026, allows exporters to use natural resource export proceeds (DHE SDA) held at 15 designated banks as collateral for rupiah loans, with interest rates left to each bank's discretion. Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) and Bank Mandiri have already applied the scheme by disbursing Rp 6 trillion in loans to PT Bukit Asam Tbk (PTBA), comprising Rp 2 trillion in working capital credit from BRI and Rp 4 trillion in DHE SDA loans from Bank Mandiri for PTBA's operational needs. Analysts project demand will concentrate among large coal, palm oil, and mineral exporters, benefiting exporters through lower-cost rupiah liquidity without releasing dollars to the forex market, while banks gain low-risk lending backed by cash deposits. Risks include currency mismatch management, potential additional collateral demands if the rupiah strengthens sharply, and competition among the 15 banks raising funding costs; HSBC Indonesia has no DHE SDA-backed financing program yet but welcomes the policy.

AUTO.title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) to Acquire Up to 4.95% of PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) via Voluntary Tender Offer at Rp 3,600 Per Share
AUTO.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) plans to acquire up to 238.4 million shares of PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO), equivalent to 4.95%, through a voluntary tender offer priced at Rp 3,600 per share, with a maximum transaction value of Rp 858.4 billion. If fully absorbed, ASII's ownership in AUTO would rise from 80% to 84.95%, with the offer period running from October 8 to November 6, 2026 and settlement scheduled for November 13, 2026. The tender price reflects a 35% premium to the 90-day average daily high price, and analysts at Trimegah Sekuritas view the move as a sign of confidence in AUTO's business rather than a step toward privatization, with free float expected to remain around 15%. AUTO's fundamentals support the outlook, with Q2-2026 net profit of Rp 592 billion, up 6% quarterly and 37% annually, alongside 19% revenue growth and aftermarket expansion through 10 distribution centers and roughly 15,000 retailers.

WIFI.body: PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk (WIFI), also known as Surge, received resignation letters from two of its board members: President Commissioner Hashim S. Djojohadikusumo and Director Henny Santoso. Hashim's resignation letter, dated 29 September 2026, was received by the company on 30 September 2026, while Henny's letter, dated 1 October 2026, was received the same day. Both resignations will take effect in accordance with applicable regulations, the company's articles of association, and a shareholders' meeting decision. WIFI will hold an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPSLB) on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, with an agenda covering changes to the composition of the Board of Commissioners and Board of Directors, as required under POJK 33/2014 within 90 days of receiving each resignation letter. AADI may also receive an additional US$550 million over the next five years depending on metallurgical coal price developments. According to BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (BRIDS), AADI indicated the proceeds will be used for domestic business development, dividends, and partial debt repayment.

AADI.title: Indonesian Stock Market Slides 6.96% in September 2026 as Analysts Recommend Stocks for October Recovery
AADI.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 6.96% month on month in September 2026, from 6,525.47 at the end of August to 6,071.13 at the end of September, pressured by the US Federal Reserve's 25 basis point rate hike to 3.75%-4.00%, a stronger US dollar, and oil prices that briefly touched US$132 per barrel. Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 1.95 trillion in a single session in early September, with PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) among the most sold stocks. Analysts recommend gradual accumulation in large-cap banking stocks including PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI), and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), gold and metal stocks PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), coal stock PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI), and consumer and plantation stocks PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT), PT Dharma Satya Nusantara Tbk (DSNG), and PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) for October 2026. Bank Indonesia held the BI-Rate at 5.75% in September to maintain exchange rate stability amid external pressures.

AADI.title: PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) to Focus on Domestic Business Development After Completing Kestrel Divestment
AADI.body: PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI), a coal issuer linked to Boy Thohir, will focus on developing its business in Indonesia after completing the divestment of shares and warrants held by its subsidiary, Adaro Capital Limited (ACL), in Kestrel Coal Group Pty Ltd (Kestrel) to Yancoal Australia Limited (Yancoal) on October 1, 2026, Melbourne time. From the divestment, AADI received approximately US$700 million, equivalent to Rp12.6 trillion (assuming an exchange rate of Rp17,970 per US$) after tax, based on the terms of the sale and purchase agreement (SPA). Under the SPA, sellers including ACL may receive contingent cash consideration if the required conditions are met. AADI plans to use the proceeds to develop the group's business in Indonesia, pay dividends, and strengthen its capital structure through partial repayment of group loans, according to President Director Julius Aslan.

AADI.title: PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) Completes Divestment of Kestrel Coal Stake to Yancoal Australia, Raising Rp14.5 Trillion
AADI.body: PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) completed the sale of its entire shares and warrants in Kestrel Coal Group Pty Ltd to Yancoal Australia Limited on October 1, 2026, executed through its subsidiary Adaro Capital Limited (ACL), in which AADI indirectly holds 90%. The transaction covered 720,385,220 ordinary shares, equal to a 47.99% stake, plus attached warrants, giving Yancoal 100% ownership of Kestrel. ACL received US$814.12 million (Rp14.57 trillion) before tax, or US$734.83 million (Rp13.15 trillion) after tax, and may receive contingent cash consideration of up to US$550 million (Rp9.85 trillion) over five years if the Platts Premium Low Vol Hard Coking Coal FOB Australia index exceeds set thresholds annually. Proceeds will fund the group's business development in Indonesia, dividend payments, and partial loan repayment, while the transaction qualifies as a Material Transaction under POJK 17/2020 without requiring shareholder approval. Proforma figures show AADI's consolidated operating profit for the six months ended June 30, 2026 rose from US$666.54 million to US$744.95 million after adjustments, while profit for the period slipped slightly from US$524.43 million to US$523.55 million due to tax and transaction-related costs.

BINA.body: Several small banks in the KBMI I and KBMI II groups continued to record business growth through August 2026 despite pressure on funding costs and asset quality challenges. DNAR.title: 26 Banks Still Below 15% Free Float Requirement; Analysts Weigh Impact on Share Prices
DNAR.body: As of August 31, 2026, 26 listed banks still have public shareholdings below the 15% free float requirement, with 10 targeting 12.5% by March 31, 2027, two targeting 15% by March 31, 2027, and 14 facing a March 31, 2029 deadline. The lowest free floats include Bank QNB Indonesia (BKSW) at 6.67%, Bank Nationalnobu (NOBU) at 7.34%, Bank Oke Indonesia (DNAR) at 7.53%, Bank Danamon Indonesia (BDMN) at 7.54%, Bank IBK Indonesia (AGRS) at 7.55%, Bank CIMB Niaga (BNGA) at 7.50%, Bank SMBC Indonesia (BTPN) at 7.87%, and Bank Syariah Indonesia (BRIS) at 9.33%, among others. Several banks are preparing corporate actions: BRIS plans a rights issue (PMHMETD II) of up to 6.8 billion Series B shares with Rp500 nominal value, projected to lift capital from Rp51.07 trillion in 2026 to Rp64.41 trillion in 2027 and CAR from 20.38% to 23.31%, with maximum dilution of 12.85% for non-exercising shareholders; CIMB Niaga, Allo Bank Indonesia (BBHI), Super Bank Indonesia (SUPA), Panin Bank, and Bank JTrust Indonesia (BCIC) are also discussing options with controlling shareholders. Analysts from Mirae Asset Sekuritas, RHB Sekuritas Indonesia, and Solstice Indonesia note that new share issuance may cause short-term EPS dilution and supply pressure, while controller share sales avoid dilution but can pressure prices, though higher free float could improve liquidity and broaden the investor base over the medium to long term; for BRIS, one option is partial share sales by shareholders Bank Mandiri (51.47%), BNI (23.24%), and BRI (15.38%).

DMAS.title: PT Puradelta Lestari Tbk (DMAS) Relies on Data Center Business, with 75% of Land Demand from the Sector
DMAS.body: PT Puradelta Lestari Tbk (DMAS), the developer of the Kota Deltamas integrated township in Central Cikarang spanning about 3,200 hectares, will continue focusing on land sales to support the data center industry trend through 2027. Around 75% of the roughly 85 hectares of industrial land demand at Kota Deltamas through mid-2026 comes from data center players, with about 16 tier-4 data center tenants already in its 300-hectare Data Center Zone. DMAS faces shrinking landbank but holds Rp 2.08 trillion in cash and equivalents as of June 2026 with no financial loans, and may pursue acquisitions of at least 500 hectares near Kota Deltamas. In the first half of 2026, DMAS revenue rose nearly threefold to Rp 1.8 trillion from Rp 613.36 billion a year earlier, while net profit jumped 175.34% to Rp 1.19 trillion from Rp 433.02 billion, and the company targets Rp 2.08 trillion in marketing sales for 2026, of which Rp 1.15 trillion (55%) was achieved in the first semester.

BKSL.title: Samuel Sekuritas Indonesia Sell Shares of Sentul City
BKSL.body: On Oct 2, 2026, Samuel Sekuritas Indonesia sold 683,885,800 Sentul City shares at IDR 72 per share, generating proceeds of IDR 49,239,777,600. DNET.title: Alfamart vs Indomaret: Comparing Profitability of Indonesia's Two Largest Minimarket Chains
DNET.body: This article compares the financial performance of Indonesia's two dominant franchised minimarket chains, Alfamart and Indomaret, for the first half of 2026. Alfamart is managed by PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT), controlled by Djoko Susanto, which posted net revenue of Rp 67.95 trillion in H1-2026, up 6.48% from Rp 63.81 trillion a year earlier, with net profit attributable to owners of the parent of Rp 2.02 trillion, up 7.4% from Rp 1.88 trillion. Indomaret is managed by PT Indomarco Prismatama, in which PT Indoritel Makmur Internasional Tbk (DNET), controlled by Anthoni Salim, holds a 40% stake; per DNET's financial statements, Indomarco recorded net sales of Rp 64.12 trillion in H1-2026 with net profit attributable to owners of the parent of Rp 943.5 billion, versus net sales of Rp 57.39 trillion and net profit of Rp 1.18 trillion in H1-2025.

JPFA.title: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk (JPFA) Sells Subsidiary Vaksindo's India and Vietnam Operations for Rp1.8 Trillion
JPFA.body: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk (JPFA) is divesting its subsidiary PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara, along with its business units in India and Vietnam, for Rp1.8 trillion. The buyers are Japfa Pte Ltd, the controlling shareholder of JPFA, together with its affiliate Bionovus Pte Ltd. Vaksindo operates in animal health, including vaccine and veterinary pharmaceutical production, as well as livestock support activities and trading. Management said the divestment allows JPFA to focus on its core businesses, monetize assets, and reinvest in feed milling, integrated poultry and aquaculture farming, and downstream meat and food processing, with part of the net proceeds serving as a source of capital expenditure.

JPFA.title: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk (JPFA) Divests PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara for Rp 1.8 Trillion to Strengthen Balance Sheet
JPFA.body: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk (JPFA) and PT Ciomas Adisatwa divested their entire 100% stake (31,000 shares) in PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara for Rp 1.8 trillion, equivalent to 8.47% of JPFA's consolidated equity as of June 2026, effective under a share purchase agreement signed on September 29, 2026. The buyers are Japfa Pte. Ltd., the controller of the Japfa Group with 56.34% ownership of JPFA, and Bionovus Pte. Ltd., keeping the transaction within the Japfa Group; the deal also transfers the Vaksindo, Vaksimune, and Vitakur trademarks from JPFA to Bionovus. JPFA said the divestment improves capital allocation efficiency and mitigates exposure to Vaksindo's higher-risk overseas expansion plans, while commercial and raw material supply arrangements with Vaksindo continue under substantially the same terms. BRI Danareksa Sekuritas analyst Abida Massi Amand noted the material cash injection improves balance sheet flexibility and maintained a buy recommendation on JPFA with a target price of Rp 2,500, while flagging that investors should monitor pricing fairness, use of proceeds, and the lost earnings contribution from Vaksindo.

JPFA.title: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk (JPFA) sells 100% of PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara for Rp1.81 trillion
JPFA.body: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk (JPFA), together with PT Ciomas Adisatwa, sold its entire 100% stake (31,000 shares) in PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara along with the VAKSINDO, VAKSIMUNE, and VITAKUR trademarks to Japfa Pte. Ltd. and Bionovus for Rp1,807 trillion, with payment due on 29 September 2026. Japfa Pte. Ltd. is JPFA's controlling shareholder with a 56.34% stake, making the deal an affiliated transaction, though the company stated it is not a material transaction under POJK 17/POJK.04/2020 and not a conflict of interest. The transaction value equals 8.47% of JPFA's consolidated equity as of 30 June 2026, and an independent appraisal by KJPP Ruky, Safrudin & Rekan valued 100% of Vaksindo and its subsidiaries at Rp1,807 trillion. JPFA said the divestment aims to make its capital structure more efficient and free up capital previously allocated to Vaksindo's mostly overseas expansion, and after the transaction it will no longer consolidate Vaksindo's revenue, profit, and assets, including its subsidiaries in India and Vietnam, while business relations on livestock raw material supply are expected to continue on substantially the same terms.

ICBP.title: Indo Premier: PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (ICBP) July-August Sales Grow 11% YoY, but Rising Raw Material Costs Pressure Margins
ICBP.body: Indo Premier Sekuritas estimates PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (ICBP) sales grew around 11% year on year in July-August 2026, supported by its instant noodle and dairy segments, with overseas sales up 21.9% yoy in the first half of 2026 aided by its Pinehill business, which operates three production facilities in Saudi Arabia. However, rising raw material costs are pressuring margins, as Bogasari raised domestic wheat prices about 5%-6% year to date and crude palm oil prices averaged up about 12.4% YTD, with wheat and CPO together accounting for roughly 45% of ICBP's COGS. Indo Premier raised its 2026 sales growth projection for ICBP to 8.4% yoy from 4.7%, but cut its 2026 and 2027 gross profit margin projections to 34.3% and 34.8% and trimmed core profit forecasts by 4.3% and 3.3%, while expecting the EBIT margin to stay within the 20%-22% guidance range. The broker maintained a buy rating on ICBP but lowered its target price to Rp 10,800 per share, based on 12 times FY2026 price-to-earnings.

ICBP.title: Government's Rp 31 Trillion Stimulus Seen Supporting Consumer Stocks AMRT, MIDI, ICBP, INDF, and MYOR
ICBP.body: The Indonesian government plans to roll out around Rp 31 trillion in economic stimulus in Q4-2026 to support household consumption, seen as a positive catalyst for consumer and retail issuers. The stimulus includes food aid of 10 kilograms of rice per month for three months for 33.24 million beneficiary families in deciles 1-4 with a budget of Rp 17.5 trillion, and wage subsidy assistance (BSU) of Rp 300,000 per month for three months for about 13.3 million workers with a budget of nearly Rp 12 trillion, plus a planned account-opening program for citizens above 17 years old in deciles 1-4. Analyst Ekky Topan of Infovesta Kapital Advisori views retail issuers AMRT and MIDI as well-positioned due to wide store networks selling daily necessities, while consumer staples issuers ICBP, INDF, and MYOR are seen as attractive for their strong brands and broad distribution. His top picks are ICBP with a target price of Rp 9,500-10,500, AMRT at around Rp 2,100, and MYOR at Rp 2,700-2,850, with a preference for gradual accumulation on strong fundamentals rather than chasing stimulus-driven rallies.

SINI.title: PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (SINI) strengthens coal mining focus while PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) acquisition talks remain ongoing

Through newly acquired subsidiary PT Kemilau Mulia Sakti (KMS), which holds a share participation in PT Cristian Eka Pratama (CEP), the holder of a production operation mining business license (IUP-OP) in West Kutai, East Kalimantan, SINI targets coal production of around 2.2 million tons in 2026, with KMS expected to contribute about Rp119 billion in revenue from July 1 to September 30, 2026. Meanwhile, negotiations over a new share acquisition plan by PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN), which currently holds a direct and indirect 27.78% stake in SINI, are still ongoing, with no definitive percentage, timeline, or signed shareholder agreement yet established.

BRIS.title: PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) Plans Rights Issue of Up to 6.8 Billion Shares
BRIS.body: PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) plans to raise capital through a rights issue (HMETD), issuing up to 6,800,000,000 Series B shares, with shareholder approval to be sought at an extraordinary general meeting scheduled for 6 November 2026. The exercise price and final share count have not been set and will be disclosed in the PMHMETD II prospectus, with completion targeted for the first quarter of 2027. All proceeds, net of issuance costs, will be used for financing distribution to support business growth, with projected capital rising from Rp 51.07 trillion in 2026 to Rp 64.41 trillion in 2027 and the capital adequacy ratio expected to improve from 20.38% to 23.31%. Shareholders who do not exercise their rights face potential dilution of up to 12.85%, and the company noted short-term profitability may be affected before recovering as funds are deployed into productive assets.

BRIS.title: PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) Prepares Right Issue to Boost Financing Capacity
BRIS.body: PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) plans a right issue (PMHMETD II), issuing up to 6.8 billion new Series B shares with a nominal value of Rp500 per share to strengthen capital and expand financing capacity. Proceeds after issuance costs will be used entirely to expand financing distribution, with equity projected to rise from Rp51.07 trillion in 2026 to Rp64.41 trillion in 2027 and the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) expected to increase from 20.38% to 23.31%. Shareholders who do not exercise their rights face dilution of up to 12.85%. The plan requires shareholder approval at an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders on Friday, 6 November 2026, with the right issue targeted for completion in the first quarter of 2027, subject to effective registration with the Financial Services Authority (OJK).

NSSS.title: Samuel Sekuritas Indonesia Sells Shares of Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera
NSSS.body: Samuel Sekuritas Indonesia sold 170,805,300 shares of Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera at IDR 770 per share, totaling IDR 131,520,081,000, and reduced its holding to 8,274,869,100 shares (34.77% ownership) from 8,445,674,400 shares (35.48%). The Oct 1, 2026 transaction is recorded as a repo redemption and continues a six‑month pattern of disposals that have cut the institution’s stake from over 45% in June to just under 35% today.

MIDI.title: Government's Rp 31 Trillion Stimulus Seen Supporting Consumer Stocks AMRT, MIDI, ICBP, INDF, and MYOR
MIDI.body: The Indonesian government plans to roll out around Rp 31 trillion in economic stimulus in Q4-2026 to support household consumption, seen as a positive catalyst for consumer and retail issuers. The stimulus includes food aid of 10 kilograms of rice per month for three months for 33.24 million beneficiary families in deciles 1-4 with a budget of Rp 17.5 trillion, and wage subsidy assistance (BSU) of Rp 300,000 per month for three months for about 13.3 million workers with a budget of nearly Rp 12 trillion, plus a planned account-opening program for citizens above 17 years old in deciles 1-4. Analyst Ekky Topan of Infovesta Kapital Advisori views retail issuers AMRT and MIDI as well-positioned due to wide store networks selling daily necessities, while consumer staples issuers ICBP, INDF, and MYOR are seen as attractive for their strong brands and broad distribution. His top picks are ICBP with a target price of Rp 9,500-10,500, AMRT at around Rp 2,100, and MYOR at Rp 2,700-2,850, with a preference for gradual accumulation on strong fundamentals rather than chasing stimulus-driven rallies.

AMMN.title: IHSG Plunges to 5,900 Level Amid Cabinet Reshuffle, Lowest in Over Two Months
AMMN.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell more than 1.61% to 5,973.16 on Thursday (October 1, 2026), its lowest level in over two months and first touch of the 5,900 zone since July 10, 2026, as President Prabowo Subianto reshuffled the Red and White Cabinet. Basic materials fell 2.72%, consumer non-primary 2.55%, and utilities 2.31%, with heavyweight decliners including PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN), PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), and PT DCI Indonesia Tbk (DCII). Foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp204.30 billion in session I, led by net sales of GOTO (Rp62.77 billion), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) (Rp29.52 billion), AMMN (Rp24.55 billion), BBRI (Rp19.80 billion), and PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) (Rp19.54 billion). The reshuffle saw Police General Listyo Sigit Prabowo appointed Presidential Chief of Staff, replacing TNI General Dudung Abdurachman, while Police General Suyudi Ario Seto became Kapolri and Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia moved to Coordinating Minister for Downstreaming and Energy.

MIKA.title: PT Mitra Keluarga Karyasehat Tbk (MIKA) Targets Around 10% Growth Through End of 2026, Backed by Private Patients
MIKA.body: PT Mitra Keluarga Karyasehat Tbk (MIKA) targets around 10% performance growth for fiscal 2026 while maintaining an EBITDA margin of 38.8%-39.5%, supported by private patients, which rose to 90% of total patients in H1 2026 from 88% a year earlier. H1 2026 revenue reached Rp 2.77 trillion, up 8% year-on-year, with average revenue per inpatient day up 12.2% to Rp 4.68 million and high-complexity service revenue up 28.6% to Rp 767 billion, or 28% of total revenue. The company plans to open its BSD hospital in Q4 2026 and an East Java hospital in Q1 2027, which may pressure margins in the short term but is seen as a medium-term growth catalyst, funded by a net cash position of about Rp 3 trillion with no debt. Analysts from BRI Danareksa Sekuritas and Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia both recommend buying MIKA shares, with target prices of Rp 2,500 and Rp 3,000 per share, respectively.

MIKA.title: PT Mitra Keluarga Karyasehat Tbk (MIKA) Strengthens Growth Through Private Patients and Expansion; Analysts Recommend Buy
MIKA.body: PT Mitra Keluarga Karyasehat Tbk (MIKA) is pursuing its growth target through end-2026, supported by higher private patient contribution and expansion of high-complexity services. In the first half of 2026, MIKA posted revenue of about Rp 2.7 trillion, up 8% year-on-year, with net profit of Rp 684 billion, up 6.9%, while high-complexity services revenue grew 28.6% to Rp 767 billion, raising its contribution to 27.7% of total revenue from 23.2% a year earlier. Private patients accounted for 90% of revenue, up from 88%, while JKN revenue fell 11.4% year-on-year, and gross margin slipped to 53.4% from 54.7% on higher use of specialist drugs, implants, and consumables. The company maintains 2026 revenue growth guidance in the low-to-mid teens with an EBITDA margin target of 38.8%-39.5%, and plans new hospitals in BSD (operational in Q4-2026) and East Java (Q1-2027), plus a nuclear medicine center and integrated oncology platform in East Java. Infovesta Kapital Advisori analyst Ekky Topan recommends buy on weakness with support at Rp 1,400-Rp 1,500 and a fundamental target of Rp 2,200-Rp 2,300, while Phillip Sekuritas analyst Helen Vincentia maintains a buy with a DCF-based target price of Rp 2,500.

TAPG.title: George Oetomo Buys Shares of Triputra Agro Persada
TAPG.body: On 2026-09-29 insider George Oetomo bought 100,000 Triputra Agro Persada shares at IDR 1,925 per share, a transaction value of IDR 192,500,000, increasing his holding to 51,006,100 shares (0.257% of the company). The purchase follows earlier September buys of 250,000 shares at IDR 2,310 and 350,000 shares at IDR 2,028.571, and a series of acquisitions since April, indicating continued insider accumulation for investment purposes.

EXCL.title: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) Posts Rp2.9 Trillion Net Profit, Up 79.6%
EXCL.body: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) recorded a net profit of US$174.35 million (around Rp2.9 trillion) in the first half of 2026, up 79.6% from US$79.08 million a year earlier, on revenue of US$1.77 billion, up 34%. Most revenue came from coal mining and trading at US$1.53 billion, while cable TV and internet services grew to US$170.49 million from US$87.15 million. DSSA completed the acquisition of PT Bali Media Telekomunikasi (BMT), which holds a 24.57% stake in PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk (EXCL), giving DSSA indirect ownership in EXCL as part of its telecommunications and digital infrastructure expansion. Its digital segment posted first-quarter revenue of US$69.1 million, up 50%, boosted by the merger of PT Eka Mas Republik (MyRepublic Indonesia) and PT Mora Telematika Indonesia Tbk (Moratelindo) into PT Ekamas Mora Republik Tbk (MoraRepublic), with a fiber optic network of over 166,000 kilometers reaching more than 12.7 million homepass. Through PT SMPlus Digital Investama (SM+), DSSA is expanding data centers, including the Jakarta SMX01 flagship which reached topping off in May 2026 and 25 Edge Data Centers, and formed PT Brilian Teknologi Sejahtera in partnership with iFLYTEK for AI and machine learning solutions.

MITI.title: Today's Stock Picks: IHSG Slips 0.83% as PT Mitra Investindo Tbk (MITI), PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA), and PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) Make Headlines
MITI.body: This stock picks roundup reports that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed lower, weakening 0.83% to 6,071.14 on Wednesday (30/9), with foreign net sell of Rp1.56 trillion in the regular market, while UNTR rose 7.55%, MORA gained 1.99%, and EMAS added 2.32%, and GOTO fell 13.51%. PT Mitra Investindo Tbk (MITI) signed an MoU on 29 September 2026 with PT CNEC Engineering Indonesia (CNEC INA), a subsidiary of China Nuclear Engineering & Construction Corporation, to develop three silica sand mining concessions held by MITI's subsidiaries, spanning exploration, feasibility studies, and technical engineering. PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA), an independent contractor for Kaltim Prima Coal (KPC) and Arutmin Indonesia, sees potential for new contracts after ESDM Minister Decree Number 365.K/2026 restricting the use of IUJP holders' subsidiaries and affiliates, which it says has no material impact on its operations. PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) set an interim cash dividend of Rp233 per share, totaling about Rp449.02 billion and equal to a 40.86% payout of its H1 2026 net profit of Rp1.10 trillion, with cum date on 8 October 2026 and payment on 26 October 2026.

MITI.title: MITI Expands Silica Mining via CNEC INA Partnership, DEWA Sees New Contract Opportunities, and AALI Declares Interim Dividend
MITI.body: MITI signed a Memorandum of Understanding with PT CNEC Engineering Indonesia (CNEC INA), a subsidiary of China Nuclear Engineering & Construction Corporation, to develop three silica sand mining concessions owned by its subsidiary, covering exploration, feasibility studies, and technical engineering with potential funding support. DEWA, an independent contractor for Kaltim Prima Coal (KPC) and Arutmin Indonesia, sees opportunities for new contracts outside current projects and stated that ESDM Ministerial Decree No. 365.K/2026 restricting use of subsidiaries and affiliates of IUJP holders has no material impact on its operations. AALI declared an interim cash dividend of Rp233 per share for fiscal year 2026, totaling about Rp449.02 billion, its highest interim dividend since 2018, reflecting a payout ratio of 40.86% on first-half 2026 net profit of Rp1.10 trillion, up 56.51% year-on-year, with a dividend yield of about 2.91% based on the Rp8,000 closing price on 30 September 2026; cum date is 8 October and payment on 26 October 2026. SRSN.title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas Recommends EMAS, UNTR, and SRSN Stocks for Thursday, October 1, 2026
SRSN.body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas issued trading recommendations for EMAS, UNTR, and SRSN on Thursday, October 1, 2026. VISI.title: TLKM and VISI Shares Fall After Extraordinary General Meetings as Analyst Weighs Prospects
VISI.body: Shares of PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) and PT Satu Visi Putra Tbk (VISI) fell on Wednesday (30/9/2026) as both companies held extraordinary general meetings (RUPSLB). TLKM closed down 3.38% at Rp2,290 after shareholders approved the second-phase spin-off of its Wholesale Fiber Connectivity business into PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia and appointed Nanang Hendarno as President Director, replacing Dian Siswarini; TLKM's H1-2026 revenue grew 3.9% yoy to Rp75.9 trillion with EBITDA up 3.8% to Rp37.5 trillion. newsLatest.title: Syndicated loan market expands 36.9% YoY to US$25.51 bn, with infrastructure and data‑center projects driving growth
newsLatest.body: Syndicated loan volume reached US$25.51 bn as of 1 Oct 2026, a 36.9% year‑on‑year increase despite a drop in the number of projects to 49 from 54. PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BNI) led the Mandated Lead Arranger list with US$4.23 bn across 20 projects, followed by PT Bank Mandiri Tbk with US$3.67 bn on 19 projects, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BRI) with US$2.40 bn on 14 projects, and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BCA) with US$1.54 bn on 13 projects. United Overseas Bank (UOB) and Oversea‑Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) recorded participation of US$1.31 bn on 9 projects and US$948.6 m on 7 projects respectively. Bank Jakarta partnered with PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (Persero) to provide Rp2.11 tn of syndicated financing for seven priority infrastructure projects in Jakarta, with Bank Jakarta contributing Rp1 tn. The article notes that infrastructure, energy, mining and especially data‑center projects are driving the strong demand for syndicated loans, though growth is expected to moderate toward year‑end.

newsLatest.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) offers premium buyback to dissenting shareholders after second‑phase spin‑off of its Wholesale Fiber Connectivity to PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia
newsLatest.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) is proceeding with the second phase of spinning off its Wholesale Fiber Connectivity segment to PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia and is offering a buyback to shareholders who oppose the spin‑off. The buyback price is set at Rp2,290 per share, a premium to the closing price of Rp2,250 on 2 Oct 2026 and above the recent low of Rp2,310 on 29 Sep 2026 after the share price fell from around Rp2,400 earlier in the week. Shareholders who do not approve the spin‑off may submit sell‑back requests between 2 Oct and 5 Oct 2026, with payment to be made within seven business days after the Ministry of Law approves the capital increase of PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia. The spin‑off became effective on 1 Oct 2026, following the RUPSLB meeting on 30 Sep 2026 where the agenda was approved.

newsLatest.title: Seven stocks, including Astra Group and Golden Energy Mines, set for cum‑dividend dates 5‑12 Oct 2026
newsLatest.body: The article announces that seven issuers will enter their cum‑dividend periods in the Regular and Negotiated markets from 5 October to 12 October 2026. The list comprises United Tractors (UNTR), Astra Graphia (ASGR), Astra Agro Lestari (AALI), Astra International (ASII) – the parent company of the Astra Group – Golden Energy Mines (GEMS) from the Sinarmas Group, Teladan Prima Agro (TLDN), and Toba Surimi Industries (CRAB), with CRAB opening on 5 October. Based on Friday’s closing prices, ASGR leads with an 11.79 % yield, followed by GEMS at 7.26 % (dividend Rp611.93 per share) and TLDN at 3.36 %; AALI, ASII, UNTR and CRAB offer yields of 2.82 %, 2.12 %, 1.65 % and 0.93 % respectively.

newsLatest.title: Three Indonesian issuers—PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR), PT Berlina Tbk (BRNA) and PT Asuransi Harta Aman Pratama Tbk (AHAP)—set to launch rights issues in October 2026
newsLatest.body: The article announces that three listed companies—PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR), PT Berlina Tbk (BRNA) and PT Asuransi Harta Aman Pratama Tbk (AHAP)—will commence rights issues in early October 2026. VKTR, the largest issuer, plans to offer up to 15 billion new shares at Rp200 each, potentially raising up to Rp3 trillion, with a 12‑for‑35 HMETD ratio and a cum date of 6 Oct, recording date of 8 Oct, and trading period 12‑23 Oct. BRNA will issue up to 543.95 million new shares at Rp685 each, targeting about Rp372.61 billion, with a 5‑for‑9 HMETD ratio, cum date 8 Oct, recording date 12 Oct, and trading 14‑21 Oct. AHAP is also listed as an issuer of a rights issue, though specific terms were not disclosed in the article. The rights issues will allow existing shareholders to purchase the new shares according to the stated HMETD allocations.

newsLatest.title: Assessing PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) stock outlook through end‑2026
newsLatest.body: The article evaluates the outlook for PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) stock up to the end of 2026. On 2 Oct 2026 the share traded at Rp 6,100, up 1.67% intraday, while YTD the price has fallen about 24% and the week shows a 2.4% correction; net foreign selling reached roughly Rp 32.1 trillion YTD. Analysts note that despite the price decline, the bank’s fundamentals remain solid with profit growth, a strong CASA base, minimal micro‑credit exposure and quarterly dividends, which they view as price‑supporting factors. The stock faces pressure from foreign fund outflows, uncertainty ahead of the MSCI review in November, and the newly introduced short‑selling mechanism, but analysts maintain a buy recommendation, citing potential upside if MSCI status, Fed rate pauses, and rupiah stability improve.

newsLatest.title: Indonesia's Richest People October 2026: Low Tuck Kwong Returns to Top with US$16.4 B Wealth
newsLatest.body: The October 2026 ranking of Indonesia’s wealthiest individuals shows Low Tuck Kwong regaining the top position. His net worth is estimated at US$16.4 billion (≈Rp291.37 trillion) and he now holds 6,951,170,541 shares, about 20,853 % of PT Bayang Resources Tbk (BYAN) after a conditional share‑purchase agreement executed by Andi Syamsudin Arsyad through PT Jhonlin Baratama. The list places Robert Budi Hartono (US$15.2 billion), Prajogo Pangestu (US$14.8 billion), Anthoni Salim of Indofood Group (US$10.8 billion), Dato Sri Tahir (US$9.4 billion), Sri Prakash Lohia (US$8.6 billion) and Otto Toto Sugiri (US$8.2 billion) in the subsequent slots. Market corrections and global commodity price swings continue to affect the asset values of these tycoons across energy, banking and mining sectors.

newsLatest.title: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) Offers Rp4.12 Trillion Bonds with Coupons up to 10%
newsLatest.body: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) is offering Obligasi Berkelanjutan V Merdeka Copper Gold Phase IV Year 2026 bonds with a principal amount of Rp4.12 trillion, as part of a continuous public offering targeting Rp15 trillion, of which Rp6.10 trillion has previously been issued. Series A bonds total Rp1.81 trillion with a fixed 8.25% annual coupon and a 367-calendar-day tenor, maturing on October 27, 2027. Series B bonds total Rp2.31 trillion with a fixed 10% annual coupon and a three-year tenor, maturing on October 20, 2029. Interest is paid quarterly, with the first payment on January 20, 2027; the offering period runs October 14-15, 2026, with listing on the Indonesia Stock Exchange expected October 21, 2026. The bonds are unsecured but backed by all of the company's assets, rank pari passu with other creditors, and the company holds an option to buy back the bonds starting one year after the allotment date.

newsLatest.title: Popular News Roundup: Boy Thohir Buys MGLV Shares, MORA Emerges as Sinar Mas Group's New Star
newsLatest.body: This roundup of the five most popular investor.id stories as of Saturday (3/10/2026) is led by Garibaldi "Boy" Thohir emerging as a shareholder of more than 1% in PT NexAI Digital Infrastruktur Tbk (MGLV) after buying 30 million shares, with MGLV up 575% year to date and closing at Rp 14,850 on Friday (2/10/2026). newsLatest.title: Foreign Investors Bought These 10 Stocks in a Week as IHSG Slid to 6,036

newsLatest.title: Foreign Investors Log Jumbo Net Sell of Rp 4.32 Trillion in a Week on Indonesian Stocks

newsLatest.title: Dian Swastatika Sentosa (DSSA) Strengthens Sinarmas Group's AI and Digital Infrastructure Ecosystem
newsLatest.body: Dian Swastatika Sentosa (DSSA), part of Sinarmas Group, reported first-half 2026 revenue of USD1.77 billion, up 34 percent year-on-year, with profit attributable to owners of the parent rising 79.6 percent to USD174.4 million. Its energy pillar, including coal mining and trading, generated USD1.53 billion in revenue, up 29.8 percent, while the technology and digital infrastructure pillar posted USD182.2 million, up 89.3 percent. Through Daya Mas Bumi Sentosa, a joint venture with FirstGen Geothermal Indonesia, DSSA is developing geothermal areas mostly outside Java, and PT Trina Mas Agra Indonesia produces domestic solar cells and modules. On the technology side, MoraRepublic expanded fiber-to-the-home coverage to 186 cities and regencies and launched MyRepublic Air fixed wireless access from Rp100 thousand per month, while SM+, with Korea Investment Real Asset Management (KIRA) and LG Sinar Mas, is completing the SMX01 AI-ready data center in Jakarta, targeted to operate in Q4 2026.

newsLatest.title: Share Buybacks Surge Toward End of 2026, With Analysts Highlighting Key Issuers
newsLatest.body: A wave of share buyback announcements by Indonesian issuers toward the end of 2026 is seen as a signal of management confidence and potential price support. Within the Astra International group, two subsidiaries announced buyback plans: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) with up to Rp 2 trillion and PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) with Rp 400 billion. Other issuers preparing buyback funds include PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) with Rp 500 billion, PT Harum Energy Tbk (HRUM) with Rp 120 billion, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) with Rp 1.38 trillion, and PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (KLBF) with Rp 500 billion. Analysts note buyback effectiveness depends on fund size relative to market capitalization and actual realization, with UNTR's move signaling undervaluation after first-semester profit fell 88.2% due to RKAB and Martabe mine issues, while TOWR is viewed as attractive at a PER of 6.5x and PBV of 0.8x with a short-term target of Rp 450-Rp 500 and long-term target of Rp 600-Rp 650.

newsLatest.title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) to Acquire Up to 4.95% of PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) via Voluntary Tender Offer at Rp 3,600 Per Share
newsLatest.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) plans to acquire up to 238.4 million shares of PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO), equivalent to 4.95%, through a voluntary tender offer priced at Rp 3,600 per share, with a maximum transaction value of Rp 858.4 billion. If fully absorbed, ASII's ownership in AUTO would rise from 80% to 84.95%, with the offer period running from October 8 to November 6, 2026 and settlement scheduled for November 13, 2026. The tender price reflects a 35% premium to the 90-day average daily high price, and analysts at Trimegah Sekuritas view the move as a sign of confidence in AUTO's business rather than a step toward privatization, with free float expected to remain around 15%. AUTO's fundamentals support the outlook, with Q2-2026 net profit of Rp 592 billion, up 6% quarterly and 37% annually, alongside 19% revenue growth and aftermarket expansion through 10 distribution centers and roughly 15,000 retailers.

newsLatest.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) has declared an interim dividend for fiscal year 2026 of Rp98 per share, totaling Rp3,895 trillion, with payment scheduled for October 30, 2026. The dividend was approved by the Board of Directors on September 10, 2026 and by the Board of Commissioners on September 30, 2026, with cum dividend dates of October 12, 2026 for the regular and negotiation markets and October 14, 2026 for the cash market, and a recording date of October 14, 2026. In fiscal year 2025, Astra distributed total dividends of Rp15.7 trillion, or Rp390 per share, comprising an interim dividend of Rp98 per share and a final dividend of Rp292 per share, equivalent to a payout ratio of about 47.8% of 2025 net profit of Rp32.76 trillion.

newsLatest.title: Analyst: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) Dividend Remains Attractive Amid Strong Credit Growth
newsLatest.body: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) is viewed as still attractive to investors for its dividend policy, with a payout ratio of about 79% of net profit for fiscal year 2025. The bank distributed around Rp44.47 trillion in dividends from fiscal 2025 net profit of Rp56.3 trillion, and set a 2026 interim dividend of Rp6.16 trillion, or Rp66 per share, bringing total dividends paid or declared across calendar 2026 to about Rp50.63 trillion. Head of Research Infovesta Utama Wawan Hendrayana said the interim dividend signals management confidence, supported by August 2026 performance showing loans and third-party funds each growing about 17.6% year on year and net profit for the first eight months of 2026 up 22.3%. He added that BMRI's valuation remains relatively fair versus analyst consensus, with the combination of dividends, profit growth, and expansion room keeping the stock in focus.

newsLatest.title: IDX Implements Short Selling and Intraday Short Selling Gradually Starting October 1, 2026
newsLatest.body: PT Bursa Efek Indonesia (IDX) stated that the implementation of Short Selling and Intraday Short Selling (IDSS) transactions is being carried out gradually, taking into account the readiness of mechanisms, infrastructure, Exchange Members, and risk management. The initial phase, effective October 1, 2026, grants IDSS facility licenses to two Exchange Members, PT Ajaib Sekuritas Asia and PT Semesta Indovest Sekuritas, and covers five stocks in the Short Selling List: ASII, BBCA, BRPT, BUMI, and INDF, selected for their high free float and liquidity. Short Selling quotas are set per Exchange Member based on average daily transaction value in the Regular Market over the prior month: members with average daily value below Rp750 billion may short sell up to 0.02 percent of listed shares per day, those between Rp750 billion and Rp1.5 trillion up to 0.03 percent, and those above Rp1.5 trillion up to 0.05 percent. IDSS investors must deposit an initial margin of at least Rp50 million or 50 percent of the Short Selling transaction value, whichever is higher, with margin adequacy monitored via the Short Selling Ratio and a forced buy mechanism executed automatically at the end of each trading day for IDSS positions; a transition period allows domestic individual investors access to Short Selling until December 31, 2026.
